shortDescription: Psycasts² — Diablo 2-style psycast skill levels, auto synergies (toggleable off), fog of war with a "show my next picks" mode, a resizable PoE constellation spec tree, seven ascension constellations, meditation→awakening→3-tier enlightenment (with a one-shot card re-deal and optional coma-free meditation), a floating Psycasters main-tab roster with arrival estimates, enemy psycaster tiers, an XML awakening trigger API, TieringOverrideDef + BalanceOverrideDef handoffs, JSON balance export/import, optional hardcore reset-lockout, a seven-page plain-language settings window, full keyed localization, celebration FX, and a PerfCache layer keeping TPS/FPS impact near zero.
body:
(spec excerpt - flat level cap, ISEKAI compat, psylink gate + random-Awakened spawn)

## ONE PICK PER PAWN, AND WHAT "AWAKENED" MEANS (2026-09-09) — Pyxis #345
Two defects behind one report: several "A flow of ancient knowledge" letters on a pawn who had not awakened, then a forced awakening with TWO card windows.

**THE DUPLICATE. `MeditationSystem.Tick` runs `RollHourly` and `AwakeningTrigger.HourlyScan` on the SAME 2500-tick boundary, one straight after the other** — and that is the whole bug. RollHourly awakens a pawn (creates the psylink, queues the pick); HourlyScan then hands the same pawn to `JoinAwaken.TryOffer`, where they match the exact signature that safety net exists to repair: psycaster, zero unlocked paths, `pendingPick == 0`, `cardPaths` empty. **`cardPaths` is written only on EMBRACE (`Window_Awakening.Confirm`), so it is empty for the entire life of an open window** — it can never stand in for "a pick is already happening". TryOffer sent its own letter and queued a second pick; `pickQueue` had no dedup and `ShowNextPick` re-validated nothing, so the second hand opened the moment the first closed. **Anything added to the hourly scan from now on has to assume RollHourly already ran this tick.**

Three layers now, all in MeditationSystem:
- **`PickInFlight(pawn)`** — true while a window is on screen (or built and waiting for the deferred Add) or a request sits in the queue. `JoinAwaken.TryOffer` checks it. Any future code that OFFERS a pick must too.
- **Per-pawn dedup in `OpenPick`** (`AcceptPick`). A queued request at a lower tier is UPGRADED in place rather than dropped, so two tiers landing on one tick cannot lose the better one. `Window_Awakening.Redeal` passes **`force: true`** — it is the one caller that legitimately re-opens for a pawn whose window is still up.
- **`MeditationData.pickResolves`, deliberately NOT scribed.** Bumped in `PostClose` for every exit (embrace, set aside, defer, forgo). Each queued request records the value it was queued at; `ShowNextPick` drops a request whose stamp has moved. Redeal's forced request skips the check, because Redeal enqueues before its own Close bumps the stamp.
- `showingForId` is an **int thingIDNumber, never a Pawn** (a static Pawn roots the dead Game graph). `GameComponent.FinalizeInit` now calls `ResetPickQueue()` instead of clearing `pickShowQueued` alone.

**"AWAKENED" IS NOT "HAS A PSYLINK".** `RollHourly`, `Accumulate` and `Enlighten` all branched on `p.Psycasts() == null`. A pawn holding a psylink they never awakened into — Empire bestowing, anima tree, scenario, or another mod (Pyxis #197, Hauts' Added Traits) — is a psycaster by that test, so they took the BREAKTHROUGH track: a free psycaster level every time the roll hit, forever, while the awakening ramp and the player's own "awakening is certain after N hours" guarantee never applied to them at all. New **`MeditationSystem.IsAwakened(pawn, med)`**: `med.awakened`, or `med.tier > 0`, or at least one unlocked path. **The unlockedPaths clause is what keeps old saves right** — a pawn who awakened before the flags existed still holds the path their card gave them. `Enlighten` only grants a breakthrough when it is true; otherwise the pawn climbs the ramp and awakens normally. The roster's milestone column follows (a path-less psycaster reports the awakening climb, not "None"). Built, NOT yet play-verified.

## CARD POOL SEED — DETERMINISTIC ON PURPOSE, AND EVERY FRESH DEAL NEEDS A TERM (2026-09-08) — Pyxis #305
`MeditationSystem.BuildPool` seeds `System.Random` from pawn state, never from the clock. That is load-bearing twice over: reloading a save before an awakening cannot be used to shop for a better hand, and a pick set aside with "Choose later" comes back as the hand the player set aside rather than a free re-roll. **So anything that is MEANT to earn a new hand has to be a term in the seed, and adding a new re-deal path without one is silent** — the pool is rebuilt correctly and lands on identical cards.
That is exactly what happened to the Tier I re-deal button: the seed read pawn id, `enlightenments`, hand size, tier and `rerollCount`, and a re-deal moves none of them. The paid `DeferReroll` only ever worked because it bumps `rerollCount`. FIX: new scribed `MeditationData.redeals`, bumped in `Window_Awakening.Redeal()` **before** `OpenPick`, folded into the seed. Scribed so a reload cannot undo a re-deal; never reset, so it stays save-scum-proof.
Two more changes to the same function. `cardPaths.Count` is now a term, so the NEXT awakening deals fresh even when `enlightenments` has not moved — repeated dev-forced awakenings on one pawn used to repeat one hand, which is how this reads during testing. And the terms are `Gen.HashCombineInt`-combined rather than summed, because the additive form let unrelated terms cancel and two different states could land on one seed; the result is masked non-negative since `System.Random(int.MinValue)` throws on Mono. Seed logic now lives in one `PoolSeed` helper. **A save holding a set-aside pick shows a different hand once after this update** — expected, the seed function changed. Not yet play-verified.

## REOPENING A SET-ASIDE PICK FROM THE ROSTER (2026-09-08) — Pyxis #307
"Choose later" used to be reachable only through `Alert_PendingCardPick`. The roster already flagged the pawn ("Path pick waiting") and gave the player nothing to click, so **"Open path cards" (`PS_BtnPick`) now leads the roster action bar whenever the selected pawn has `pendingPick > 0`.** Same handoff as the alert: zero `pendingPick`, hand the tier to `MeditationSystem.OpenPick`, then `PsycasterRoster.Invalidate()` (which is frame-safe by design — it refuses to rebuild during the frame it arrives). **The reopened hand is the SAME hand**, because nothing on this path touches the pool seed; a reopen must never become a free re-roll.
**Whether the button shows is answered ONCE PER FRAME and held** (`pickFrame` vs `Time.frameCount`, `pickShown`). Reading `pendingPick` live would draw the button on a frame's early passes and skip it on the passes after MouseUp cleared the value — the control count then changes inside one frame, which is the settings-page blanking bug in a new place. `Time.frameCount` is constant across the passes of one frame, which is what makes it the right key.
**The action bar's left group is now priority-ordered and fit-tested.** Each button draws only if it still fits before the Jump button (anchored right). The bar already overlapped itself below roughly 840px window width against a 700px minimum, and a fifth button would have widened that gap; dropping the least important button is what the Paths column already does below 900px. Order: Open path cards (only when waiting) · Open psycast tab · Constellation · Set default focus, with Jump to pawn pinned right.

## AWAKENING CARD RE-DEAL + THE WINDOW-ADD HAZARD (2026-09-07) — Pyxis #264
**Tier I only: "Discard these cards and deal a new set".** Gate (revised 2026-09-08): `tier <= 1 && !redealt && cardRedeal && chosen >= 0 && flipT[chosen] >= 0.999f`, PLUS, when `cardRevealAll` is on, every card in the hand face up. The original all-face-down gate was wrong the other way (rerolling a hand you have not seen tells you nothing); the all-face-up gate replaced a middle state where, in reveal-all, a Reroll sat beside one turned card and two face-down ones and read as 'reroll this card'. In commit-on-flip mode the first turn IS the pick and no other card can ever be turned, so all-face-up is unreachable and the turned pick stays the gate there — requiring the whole hand would delete the button on default settings. ONE per awakening. **Free by design**: the tier II/III `DeferReroll` costs a meditation cycle plus coma risk, and charging the same for an immediate re-deal would make that option strictly worse. **One rather than unlimited** because unlimited turns the card draw into "pick any path", which is the opposite of what the card system is for.
Implemented as close-and-reopen through `MeditationSystem.OpenPick`, so the new hand uses the same `BuildPool` rules (count, meditation-focus theming, tier) instead of a second copy of that logic — **but see the seed section above: reusing BuildPool is not enough on its own, the seed has to move too.** The enqueue MUST happen before `Close()`, because `PostClose` is what ends in `ShowNextPick()`. It also passes `force: true` now, since the per-pawn duplicate guard would otherwise refuse it. The one-use marker is a **static `int` thingIDNumber, never a Pawn reference** — the replacement window does not exist yet when `Redeal` runs so the flag cannot be handed over directly, and a static Pawn would root a dead Game graph. `Confirm()` releases it.

**THE HAZARD THIS EXPOSED — read before touching any window that opens another window.** Seen once in run #6 as a **root-level OnGUI NullReferenceException with a truncated stack naming only vanilla** (`UIRoot_Play.UIRootOnGUI` / `Verse.Root.OnGUI`), which is what this class of bug always looks like: the real frames are eaten by Verse's root handler, so the log attributes it to RimWorld and tells you nothing. Vanilla `WindowStack.TryRemove` runs `window.PostClose()` **after** `windows.Remove(window)` but **before** it repairs `focusedWindow`, all while `WindowStackOnGUI` is walking that same list by index. Adding a window from inside `PostClose` corrupts the walk. NOT new — the multi-pawn pick chain always did this — but it previously needed two pawns awakening in the same moment; the button made it one click.
FIX: `ShowNextPick` builds the window but hands the `Find.WindowStack.Add` to **`LongEventHandler.ExecuteWhenFinished`**, landing it next frame, outside both the removal and the GUI walk. `MeditationSystem.pickShowQueued` stops a second call in the same frame dealing twice (`IsOpen` is still false until the deferred Add runs), and `GameComponent.FinalizeInit` clears it — a latched flag would block every future pick for the whole process, and statics outlive a Game. **NOT yet play-verified.**

## COMA-FREE MEDITATION (2026-09-07) — Pyxis #262
`comaSafeHours` slider max raised 16 → 24. At 24 the label switches to `PS_SetSafeWindowOff` and the coma-risk slider is hidden (snapshotted before the slider draws, per the frame-pass rule).
**Widening the slider was NOT enough, and this is the part to remember.** The risk is three terms: `max(0, todayHours - safe) * risk` + `max(0, streakHours - safe) * risk * 0.5` + `rerollCount * 0.06`. Only the FIRST dies at 24h — `streakTicks` counts unbroken meditation and is not reset daily, so a continuously-meditating pawn crosses 24h and keeps rolling, and the deferred-reroll term never depended on the window at all. So `PsycastSynergiesSettings.ComaRiskOff` (`comaSafeHours >= 24f`) skips the WHOLE roll in `MeditationSystem`, rather than trusting the arithmetic. MeditationBars follows: coma row reads `PS_BarComaOff` ("None") over an empty green bar with `PS_BarComaTipOff`, instead of a bar the player can never fill.

## UNLOCK BURST (2026-09-07) — Pyxis #263. The invest FX was never broken.
Reported as "the unlock animation stopped working". It had never existed. Investing fires `SkillFx.OnSkillInvest` from both `Dialog_ConfirmInvest` and the shift-click path and was intact throughout (confirmed in game). **Learning** a psycast goes through VPE's own click into `CompAbilities.GiveAbility`, and our code silently baselined it to level 1 without telling SkillFx. Under the old fog default the "?" cover lifting WAS the visual; with `fogRevealNext` the psycast is already visible, so unlocking changed nothing on screen.
FIX in `Patch_DrawAbility.EnsureFrame`: diff the learned set between consecutive frames of the SAME pawn and fire `Grade.Invest` for anything new, one sound per frame if several arrive at once (neurotrainers, dev). **Seeded without firing on the first frame a pawn is seen** — otherwise opening the tab on an established psycaster sprays bursts over their whole tree. Cannot fire during pawn generation because it only runs while icons are drawing. No new Harmony patch. Both bursts play-verified run #6.

## SETTINGS WINDOW REBUILT (2026-09-07) — left rail, seven pages, plain-language rewrite
Replaces the five-across gold tab strip. **Vanilla chrome only, by explicit user instruction: no accent bars, no custom-coloured tab boxes, no left-edge highlight stripe.** `Widgets.DrawHighlightSelected` for the active row, `Widgets.DrawHighlight` on hover, `Widgets.DrawLineVertical` as the separator, `GameFont.Medium` white section heads over `GapLine`. Rail is 176px, rows 32px, content starts at rail + 20px.

**Seven pages** (`SettingsTabs` entries are key suffixes, `PS_SetTab_<entry>`): Psycast levels · Paths and points · Meditation · Pilgrimages · Enemy psycasters · Display · Advanced. The old Skills page was split three ways — display toggles to **Display**, level cap / ISEKAI / synergy graph / balance edits to **Advanced**, the rest stayed as **Psycast levels**.

**`l.maxOneColumn = true` IS MANDATORY HERE.** `Listing_Standard` breaks into a second column the moment content passes `listingRect.height`, and `NewColumn()` resets `curY` to 0 while pushing `curX` a full column right — outside the scroll group, invisible. The height feedback loop then finishes it: `settingsTabH[tab] = l.CurHeight + 24` reads the just-reset `curY`, so next frame's viewRect is tiny, the break happens one row in, and **the page collapses to nothing but its first section head, with no exception and nothing in the log**. Dormant until the pages outgrew the 1200px first-frame guess, which giving every setting a description line did immediately. Also: viewRect height is floored at `body.height`, and the first-frame guess is 3000. Written up in the app's `ui` lore.

**Every setting carries an always-visible plain-English line under it** (`Hint`), and the tooltips those replaced are gone. Hint font is `Text.TinyFontSupported ? Tiny : Small`, **measured and drawn in the same font** (Text.Font's setter silently substitutes Small when tiny text is off).

**`Listing.Indent` only moves curX, it does NOT narrow the column** — a rect drawn after it overruns the scrollbar. `PushSub`/`PopSub` shift the cursor AND drop `ColumnWidth` by the same 24px, then restore both. Sub-settings (link %, cost %, spawn chance, level cap value, enemy tiers, breakthrough sliders, fog "next picks") sit inside those.

**"Disable synergies" is shown the way round a player reads it** — the checkbox says "Psycasts feed each other" and writes `!linksOn` back into `disableSynergies`. The frame-start snapshot rule is unchanged and still load-bearing: every toggle-gated row reads its visibility into a local BEFORE the checkbox draws.

**Language rules applied throughout PS_Settings.xml**: no em/en dashes, no "&", no "respec". Also banned this pass at the user's request: AI register and jargon. Gone: "authoritative", "non-destructive", "diagnostic escape hatch", "geometric diminishing returns", "anti-farming", "the control set", "layered on top of", "directed, role-based synergies". "High performance caching" is now "Remember recent calculations". **Write new settings strings in this register.**

## FOG OF WAR: "SHOW MY NEXT PICKS" (2026-09-07) — new sub-mode, default ON
`fogRevealNext` (scribed, default true), shown under the fog checkbox on the Display page. When fog is on and this is on, a psycast whose prerequisites are already met stays fully visible; only what sits deeper gets the "?" cover. `Patch_DrawAbility.PrereqsMet` mirrors VPE's `AbilityExtension_Psycast.PrereqsCompleted` (empty prerequisite list = always reachable, otherwise ANY prerequisite is enough) but reads the existing per-frame `fLearned` set instead of rescanning `LearnedAbilities` per icon. Root psycasts have no prerequisites, so the bottom of every tree is always readable. Cover is still Repaint-only with no ButtonInvisible, so VPE's click-to-unlock passes through. **Side effect worth knowing: this removed the only visual the unlock moment had — see the unlock-burst section.**

## FOCUS-TYPE GIZMO REMOVED FROM THINGS (2026-09-07)
`CompSchoolFocus.CompGetGizmosExtra` is gone. The comp is patched onto every `CompProperties_MeditationFocus` / `CompProperties_UsesMeditationFocus` ThingDef, so in practice EVERY sculpture, brazier, throne, anima tree and meditation spot carried a "Focus type: ..." button. The same choice already lives on the pawn in three places (Psycasters main tab, the psycast tab's focus row, Modern Psycasts UI's focus tiles), so a colonist carries their preference to whatever they sit at.
`selectedFocus` is **kept and still scribed**, and `MeditationSystem`'s priority chain still reads it FIRST (building attunement > pawn default > building's native focus), so saves that attuned something keep behaving as before. `CompInspectStringExtra` prints the focus-type line only when `selectedFocus != null`. Keys `PS_FocusTypeDesc` and `PS_FocusAnyTrait` deleted. `CompSchoolFocus` also gained `[StaticConstructorOnStartup]` (static Texture2D fields; Verse warned every run).
**The two remaining pawn gizmos were deliberately kept**: the ascension aura toggle and "Stop meditating" (only while forced continuous meditation runs — it must stay reachable on the pawn).

## DUPLICATE SKILL TOOLTIP — FIXED (2026-09-07). Pyxis #243.
Users saw VPE's plain tooltip AND our styled skill card at once. `Patch_SuppressVpeAbilityTip` prefixed `TooltipHandler.TipRegion(Rect, Func<string>, int)` — a **three-instruction wrapper** whose entire body is `TipRegion(rect, new TipSignal(...))`. **Mono inlines methods that small, so the prefix never ran at inlined call sites.** Both VPE's `ITab_Pawn_Psycasts.DoAbility` and Modern Psycasts UI's `DoAbility` call exactly that overload. FIX: target `TipRegion(Rect, TipSignal)` — the real sink, 19 lines, never inlined, and the method every other overload funnels through. `ShouldSuppress` also moved off Unity's exact-float `Rect ==` to a half-pixel tolerance, with `suppressFrame != Time.frameCount` kept as the first cheap gate because this prefix now runs for EVERY tooltip in the game. **Never patch a trivial forwarding wrapper; patch what it forwards to.**

## TEXTURE REGENERATION — ATTEMPTED 2026-09-06, REJECTED. Pyxis #189. DO NOT REPEAT BLIND.
A full regeneration of all 71 textures in vanilla style was tried with the texture lab and rejected by the user on inspection ("way too far away from vanilla"). The pilot (4 subjects x 2 variants) and its findings are preserved because re-running this from scratch would cost the same and reach the same place.

- **Provider reality on this machine: OpenAI only.** Gemini and xAI have no API key. That matters beyond cost — **OpenAI is the only provider that honours `transparent`**, so if that key ever changes, every UI glyph comes back on an opaque rectangle and is unusable.
- **Output is capped at 128x128 regardless of the `size` argument.** The style profile's own size convention ("typically 128x128 px, about 128 px per tile") is written verbatim into the generated prompt and the model obeys it. This is a RESOLUTION DOWNGRADE for `Things/PS_PilgrimAltar.png` (256) and would destroy `UI/CardBack.png` (950x1515) and `UI/SpecTreeMap.png` (880x930). Untested levers: an explicit size written into the subject text, and `size: "2K"`.
- **`vanilla-core-authored` is `[described]`, n=0 — never measured.** Verified the reason first-hand: `Data/` holds only **7 loose PNGs**; all Core/DLC art is inside `RimWorldWin64_Data/resources.assets` + the 254 MB `.resS`. **No unpacker exists on this machine** — no AssetStudio, no AssetRipper, no UnityPy, and the only global dotnet tool is `ilspycmd`. Building a real `[extracted]` profile needs an operator to export Texture2D into a folder. That is also the honest fix for the 128px cap, since real vanilla carries 256+ size buckets.
- **The image model is the WRONG TOOL for 63 of the 71 files, independent of profile quality — demonstrated, not predicted.** The 50 `UI/Specs/*` glyphs are flat single-colour icons drawn at 24-48px and recoloured at runtime via `GUI.color`; the candidate came back a painted swirl with rocks, which tints to mud. The FX sprites (`FX/Ascension/*`, `UI/Sparkle`, `UI/Glow`) are alpha ramps that are **additively blended**; the candidate came back baked gold **with a dark outline**, and a dark outline under additive blending adds grey haze instead of glow. If these are ever redone, **SVG is the tool**.
- Only 8 files were ever good candidates. Of the pilot, the altar and `Pilgrim_Altar` were genuinely better in STYLE and still rejected on fidelity.
- **Nothing was overwritten, ever** — `generate_texture` refuses to replace an existing file. The 8 rejected candidates sit in `.circinus/texture-candidates/`, **moved OUT of `Textures/` because that directory ships whole to the Workshop.**
- **Tooling kept:** `.circinus/mockups/build-compare.sh` regenerates `texture-compare.html`. **The mockup sandbox blocks local file loads, so relative `<img src>` renders NOTHING; the script inlines all 91 images as base64.** A white-on-transparent sprite also looks blank in any preview — that is what the checkerboard tiles are for.

## PSYCASTER ROSTER MAIN TAB (2026-09-06) — replaces the dormant psycast tab. PLAY-VERIFIED.
`MainTabWindow_Psycasters` + `Defs/MainButtons.xml` (`PS_Psycasters`, order 95, `validWithoutMap=true`). Always visible; no setting gates it.

**ICON HIDES THE LABEL.** `MainButtonWorker.DoButton` does `label = def.Icon == null ? text : ""` and draws the icon at a fixed **32x32 centred** — so a main-button icon must read at 32px, and the word "Psycasters" only appears in the hover tooltip. Art is a white-on-transparent silhouette authored as SVG at 128x128 via `render_svg_to_png`.

**It is a FLOATING window, not an anchored tab.** `draggable`, `resizeable`, `doCloseX` in the ctor, and `SetInitialSizeAndPosition` deliberately does **NOT** call base — `MainTabWindow.SetInitialSizeAndPosition` is what welds a main tab to a screen edge, and calling base then fixing up x/y afterwards was the first attempt's bug. The rect lives in settings (`rosterX/Y/W/H`, saved in `PostClose` only when it moved) and is clamped back on-screen on load. Vanilla's `WindowResizer.minWindowSize` floor is 150x150 and `Window.resizer` is PRIVATE, so the minimum is an idempotent clamp (700x360) in `DoWindowContents` — a floor, not an increment, so repeating it across a frame's passes is safe.

**Columns**: Pawn · Tier · Level · Paths (dropped below 900px) · Meditation · Next milestone (caption + value over a 6px bar) · Expected. Sentence case, PawnTable-style header band, alternating row tint, selection is a FLAT highlight (**no left-edge accent — rejected twice in review**), no avatars. Groups: Psycasters / On the path to awakening / Not progressing. Action bar (see the reopen section for its layout rule): Open path cards (only while one is waiting) · Open psycast tab · Constellation · Set default focus · Jump to pawn. Double-click = open psycast tab. View prefs `rosterIncludeCaptives` (ON) / `rosterHideIncapable` (OFF) live in settings with no settings row.
**The milestone column reads awakening progress for a psycaster who holds no path** (an outside psylink the system never adopted), because as of 2026-09-09 those pawns really are on the awakening ramp — it used to print "None".

**Psyfocus / neural heat / sensitivity were REMOVED at the user's call** — live combat numbers that belong on the pawn's own tab and said nothing about "who is climbing and when do they arrive". Do not add them back without asking.

**Scope: NO ENEMIES, EVER.** Free colonists (all maps + caravans), plus prisoners and slaves when `rosterIncludeCaptives`. Quest lodgers excluded; non-psycasters under 13 excluded.

**Prisoners and slaves are DISPLAY ONLY and this is deliberate.** `MeditationSystem.Accumulate`/`RollHourly` filter `HostFaction == null`, and BOTH have a HostFaction, so neither accrues. They are listed because a captured pawn may ALREADY be a psycaster. Extending accrual to them is a gameplay change and needs a setting.

**Arrival estimates — `MeditationData.medDayAvg` + `medDays` (scribed).** Folded in at the existing 60000-tick daily reset BEFORE `todayTicks` is zeroed: `medDayAvg = medDays == 0 ? todayTicks : Lerp(medDayAvg, todayTicks, 0.35f)` (~6-day EMA). No new tick cost. Empty days decay it so a lapsed pawn's estimate fades. ETA = remaining ÷ medDayAvg. **With no rate at all we print "No estimate" / "Storyteller only" — never a guessed date.**

**Two IMGUI hazards handled — do not regress:** (1) `Invalidate()` records `dirtyFrame` and `EnsureBuilt` refuses to rebuild during that frame, because a mid-frame rebuild changes the ROW COUNT between passes of one frame; (2) rows are **not** culled to the visible scroll band, since scroll position can move between passes and a visibility test would register a different control count per pass. The action bar's conditional button follows the same law by a third route (per-frame snapshot). All row strings are precomputed in the model build. Whole draw is try/catch → `Log.Warning`.

**REMOVED in the same pass: the always-on psycast tab.** `Patch_DormantTab.cs` deleted, the `alwaysShowPsycastTab` setting deleted, the six `PS_Dormant*` keys deleted. Awakened psycasters unaffected: every one of those patches early-returned on `DormantTab.Enabled`, so VPE's own `IsVisible`/`UpdateSize`/`FillTab` simply resume.

**Also fixed there:** `SkillFx` gained `[StaticConstructorOnStartup]`. **Any type in this mod with a static Texture2D field needs that attribute** (SkillFx, Patch_AuraToggleGizmo, CompSchoolFocus).

## PILGRIMAGE LIFECYCLE OVERHAUL (2026-09-06) — Pyxis #155 / #176 / #175
Four changes. Three close permanent-lockout paths; the fourth is a balance correction. The shared symptom: a pilgrimage quest stuck in `QuestState.Ongoing` forever, which makes `PilgrimQuestOngoing(tier)` report a pilgrimage in flight for the rest of the save and suppress every future pity offer at that tier, colony-wide. **Any future change that can leave a pilgrimage quest Ongoing reproduces this whole class of bug.**

**1. The End() overload bug (#155) — VERIFIED FIXED IN GAME (altar chain).** All four termination paths called `quest.End(outcome, sendStandardLetter: true)`. The runtime method is `Quest.End(QuestEndOutcome, bool sendLetter, bool playSound)`. No instance overload has a parameter named `sendStandardLetter`, so overload resolution silently bound to the **extension** `QuestGen_End.End` — a generation-time helper that does `QuestGen.quest.AddPart(...)`. `QuestGen.quest` is null outside generation → NRE from inside `QuestPartTick`, before the quest ever ended. `firedEnd = true` latched BEFORE the throwing call and the site was destroyed on the line above, so the exception fired exactly ONCE and every later tick short-circuited — no repeating error, nothing in the log. Success was broken identically, so the FIRST pilgrimage a save resolved was the last possible at that tier. FIX: `PilgrimQuestEnd.End(quest, outcome)` — single choke point, guards `State == Ongoing`, calls `quest.End(outcome, sendLetter: true)`. **NEVER reintroduce the `sendStandardLetter:` named argument.**

**2. Stuck-save recovery.** Both tick guards are now `if (firedEnd) { RetryStuckEnd(); return; }`, self-limiting. New scribed `endedWith` carries the intended outcome; pre-fix saves conclude as `Unknown`.

**3. Anima chain lockout (#176) — NOT the same bug. BUILT, NOT YET PLAY-VERIFIED.** `QuestPart_PilgrimJourney.QuestPartTick` only bailed on `sites.Count == 0`, but sites are destroyed IN PLACE and never removed, so Count never drops. `TimeoutComp` only spares a site that currently HAS a map, so while the pilgrim is at site 1 the others run down their own 60-day timers and the first to expire makes the journey unwinnable while the part keeps ticking. FIX: fail when a site is gone **AND still incomplete**. The "still incomplete" half is load-bearing — a COMPLETED site disappearing is expected, so keying on "destroyed" alone would false-fail every successful journey at its second site.

**4. Refire (#175).** (a) `TryFirePilgrimPity` used to clear `pilgrimTicks` when the offer was MADE rather than when it succeeded, so a missed site cost the whole guarantee window. Line removed: `SetTier` already zeroes it on any tier change, so success still discharges it while failure refunds the climb. (b) `PilgrimQuestGen.BailOut` attaches a `QuestPart_QuestEnd` on all four root-node bail paths — QuestGen has ALREADY created the quest by the time `RunInt` runs, so a bare `return` left a part-less quest: accepted, never ticked, unendable. **Both classes carry comments distinguishing generation-time `QuestPart_QuestEnd` from runtime `Quest.End` — conflating them is what caused #155.**

**Storyteller vs pity:** `TestRunInt` does NOT consult `PilgrimQuestOngoing`, so the storyteller path was never blocked. Only the PITY path was killed outright.

## PERFORMANCE LAYER (2026-07-24 quadruple pass) — PerfCache.cs + layered def caches
- **PerfCache**: tick/frame-scoped memo stores for StatMultiplier, CostMultiplier, MaxLevel (packs psy into the value), ChargeStore.Max, TierOf. Stamp = (frameCount, TicksGame, Version); ANY component change clears all stores. Key = pawnId<<32 | shortHash<<8 | slot (collision-free, alloc-free). `PerfCache.Bump()` MUST be called at every same-frame mutation site — GameComponent SetLevel/ClearPawn/ResetPawn, SetTier, PsycastInfo.ClearCaches, Mod.WriteSettings, Window_Specializations commit + resets, FinalizeInit. Gated by `perfCaching` (Display page, "Remember recent calculations"). LangCache = language-guarded Translate cache.
- **PsycastInfo layered def-stable caches** (never cleared; pure functions of the def): L0 ArchFlags, L1 RoleOf, L2 IsSingleStrike, L3 HasStat bitmask, plus PsyExtOf/PathOf. LAYERING RULE: each compute only calls lower layers or HasStatUncached — RoleOf's three probes MUST stay on HasStatUncached (cycle otherwise). Masks built at startup from AUTHORED def values, immune to CastScaling's temporary field mutation.
- **Effective caches** (cleared by ClearCaches): effPrim/effPrimStr/effEdge/effEdgeStr + grantsMultiCache.
- **Instance cache**: `GameComponent.Instance` cached per Game reference; null never latched; refs CLEARED when `Current.Game` is null (else the static roots the dead Game graph).
- **SpecEffects overloads** take SpecData; ComputeStatMultiplier resolves GetSpec ONCE.
- **UI**: SkillTooltip precomputes ALL draw strings; model cache key includes PerfCache.Version. Patch_DrawAbility uses the gated `SkillFx.Draw(rect, pawn, def)` overload. MeditationBars caches strings on a 60-tick quantum + language. **MainTabWindow_Psycasters follows the same rule: every string a row draws is built in the throttled model rebuild, never in Draw.**
- **Tick**: MeditationSystem.Tick takes the component. HediffComp_AscensionFx reads the aura toggle every 15 ticks. ChargeStore sweeps dead pawns every 120 ticks; CastScaling amp windows likewise — three leak classes closed.
- Staleness contract: worst case ONE frame/tick for unbumped paths. When adding ANY new mutation of skill levels, spec ownership, tier, or balance layers: call `PerfCache.Bump()`.
